'''Peyton Robert Siva, Jr.''' (born October 24, 1990)<ref name=UofLSportsProfile>{{cite web |url=http://www.gocards.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/siva_peyton00.html |title=Peyton Siva Bio |work=gocards.com |accessdate=May 17, 2013}}</ref> is an American former [[college basketball]] player and current NBA prospect.

==Early life==
Siva, of [[Samoan American|Samoan]] descent, grew up in a troubled Seattle neighborhood near the intersection of three gang territories. His mother worked three jobs to try to support the family. His father was mostly absent, struggling with drug and alcohol addiction throughout Siva's childhood, and was frequently jailed on drug charges. His older siblings, a brother and a sister, also had many brushes with the law, with his sister regularly being caught shoplifting. At age 13, by which time he had taught himself to drive, he went out to look for his missing father and found him in a drug den with a gun, and contemplating suicide. The younger Siva successfully talked his father out of killing himself. Young Siva also had a Primary-High School sweet heart Lome Manufekai who now lives in Brooklyn, New York. <ref name=Saslow>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/8576564/louisville-pg-peyton-siva-returns-senior-season-lead-cardinals-espn-magazine |title=The ascent from deuce-8 |first=Eli |last=Saslow |publisher=''[[ESPN The Magazine]]'' |date=November 12, 2012 |accessdate=November 1, 2012}}</ref><!--Will appear in print November 12.-->

Siva, determined to escape the fate of other family members, plunged himself into Sport. When he first tried out for youth football, he was too light to play, but managed to make weight by stuffing his pockets with decks of playing cards and several cell phones. He soon developed a reputation as a relentlessly aggressive athlete in both football and basketball, and as a promising young prospect. Siva also made it a point to avoid alcohol and drugs, and helped many other boys in his neighborhood avoid gang involvement, partially by persuading his mother to let them stay at her house on weekends.<ref name=Saslow/>

==High School==
Siva attended [[Franklin High School (Seattle, Washington)with Rob Will.|Franklin High School]] in Seattle. His freshman year he averaged 13.5 points helping Franklin win the 4A championship.  As a senior  he averaged 18.1 points, 5.3 assists, 3.4 rebounds, and 2.3 steals,<ref name="UofLSportsProfile" /> leading Franklin to the Class 3A state championship.<ref name="HS-POY">{{cite news |url=http://seattletimes.nwsource.com/html/localnews/2009063706_apbkhwashallstateteam1stldwritethru.html |title=Siva and Moore unanimous AP players of the year  |accessdate=2011-02-02 |last= |first= |coauthors= |date= 2009-04-15|work= |publisher=Seattle Times}}</ref>  He was a unanimous selection for AP Washington Player of the Year,<ref name="HS-POY"/> was named a [[McDonalds All-American]],<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.seattlepi.com/preps/400795_prepbok20.html |title=Siva headlines state contingent for McDonald's All-American Game
 |accessdate=2011-02-02 |last= Fessenden|first= Darren|coauthors= |date= 2009-02-19|work= |publisher=[[Seattle P-I]]}}</ref> and was named [[Washington Mr. Basketball|Mr. Basketball]] in the state of Washington.<ref name="UofLSportsProfile"/>

==College==

===Freshman year===
During his [[2009-10 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Freshman season]] Siva averaged 11.3 minutes in 31 games backing up senior starter [[Edgar Sosa (basketball)|Edgar Sosa]]. <ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/player/gamelog/_/id/45951/year/2010/peyton-siva |title=Peyton Siva Stats, News, Videos, Highlights, Pictures, Bio – Louisville Cardinals – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=1990-10-24 |accessdate=2013-04-09}}</ref>  Hampered by a wrist injury throughout the year he managed to dish out at least 3 assists in 11 games and he scored a career high 14 at West Virginia. Louisville beat #1 [[2009–10 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]] 78–68 in their final game of the final season at [[Freedom Hall]], before moving to the [[KFC Yum! Center]]. <ref>{{cite web|author=2:00 PM ET, March 6, 2010Freedom Hall, Louisville, KY |url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300650097 |title=Syracuse Orange vs. Louisville Cardinals – Recap – March 06, 2010 – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=2010-03-06 |accessdate=2013-04-09}}</ref> The Cardinals finished the season 20–13, and tied for 5th in the [[Big East Conference (1979–2013)|Big East]] with a 11–7 conference record. They lost in the second round of the [[2010 Big East Men's Basketball Tournament|Big East Tournament]] to [[2009–10 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team|Cincinnati]] 66–69. <ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/boxscore?gameId=300690097 |title=Cincinnati Bearcats vs. Louisville Cardinals – Box Score – March 10, 2010 – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=2010-03-10 |accessdate=2013-04-09}}</ref> Louisville received an at-large bid to the [[2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2010 NCAA Tournament]], earning a 9 seed in the South Region where they lost to 8 seed [[2009–10 California Golden Bears men's basketball team|California]] 62–77 in the first round. <ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/boxscore?gameId=300780025 |title=Louisville Cardinals vs. California Golden Bears – NCAA Tournament Game – Box Score – March 19, 2010 – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=2010-03-19 |accessdate=2013-04-09}}</ref>

web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/player/gamelog/_/id/45951/year/2011/peyton-siva |title=Peyton Siva Stats, News, Videos, Highlights, Pictures, Bio – Louisville Cardinals – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=1990-10-24 |accessdate=2013-04-09}}</ref> His averaged 9.9 points per game and his 5.2 assists per game ranked second best in the Big East.<ref name="University of Louisville">{{cite web|title=2011–12 Louisville Basketball Media Guide|url=http://www.guide.provations.com/louisville/2011mensbasketball#pg64|work=Player Bio: Peyton Siva|publisher=University of Louisville|accessdate=29 January 2012}}</ref> In consecutive games against [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]] and [[2010-11 Connecticut Huskies men's basketball team|Connecticut]], Siva hit game-winning layups in the final seconds to give Louisville one-point victories.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310260097 |title=Peyton Siva's layup helps Louisville tip West Virginia |accessdate=2011-02-02 |last= |first= |coauthors= |date= |work= |publisher=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310290041 |title=Peyton Siva outshines Kemba Walker as Louisville edges Connecticut |accessdate=2011-02-02 |last= |first= |coauthors= |date= |work= |publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> He was an honorable mention selection for the 2011 All-Big East Men's Basketball Team<ref>{{cite web|title=All-BIG EAST Men's Basketball Teams Announced|url=http://www.bigeast.org/News/tabid/435/Article/221858/all-big-east-mens-basketball-teams-announced.aspx|work=All-BIG EAST Men's Basketball Teams Announced|publisher=Big East Conference|accessdate=28 January 2012}}</ref> and was named to the [[2011 Big East Men's Basketball Tournament]] All-Tournament Team after averaging 12 points, 7.7 assists, and 5.3 rebounds as the Cardinals reached the championship game.<ref name="University of Louisville"/> The Cardinals finished the season 25–10, 12–6 in the [[2010–11 Big East Conference men's basketball season|2010–11 Big East season]] tied for 3rd in the conference. They received an at-large bid and a #4 seed in the [[2011 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2011 NCAA Tournament]] where they were upset in the second round by #13 seeded [[2010–11 Morehead State Eagles men's basketball team|Morehead State]] 61–62. <ref>{{cite web|author=1:40 PM ET, March 17, 2011Pepsi Center, Denver, CO |url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310760097 |title=Morehead State Eagles vs. Louisville Cardinals – NCAA Tournament Game – Recap – March 17, 2011 – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=2011-03-17 |accessdate=2013-04-09}}</ref>

===Junior year===
During his junior year in [[2011-12 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|2011–12]], Siva had difficulties on the court early in the season; midway through the season, he had made less than 25% of his three-point attempts, and turned the ball over as much as four times in one half.<ref name=Saslow/> Cardinals coach [[Rick Pitino]] sensed that Siva was getting involved in too many things, and pulled him aside for a talk. Pitino later recalled, "I told him, 'Take a relationship sabbatical — I'll even call your girlfriend for you.' He should only be making time for two things: school and basketball. I told him that we need 100 percent of his focus on the court."<ref name=Saslow/> From that point, Siva rediscovered his game, and became the Most Outstanding Player of the [[2012 Big East Men's Basketball Tournament|2012 Big East tournament]]. In the tournament he averaged 13.8 points and 5.8 assists per game. Louisville advanced to the Final Four of the [[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2012 NCAA Tournament]], upsetting #1 seed [[2011–12 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] 57–44 in the sweet sixteen and defeating #7 seed [[2011–12 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]] in the regional final. Before losing in the national semifinals to [[Kentucky–Louisville rivalry|arch-rival]] and eventual national champion [[2011–12 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]]. <ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/player/gamelog/_/id/45951/year/2012/peyton-siva |title=Peyton Siva Stats, News, Videos, Highlights, Pictures, Bio – Louisville Cardinals – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=1990-10-24 |accessdate=2013-04-09}}</ref> Siva averaged 9.1 points, 3.2 rebounds, 5.6 assists, and 1.7	steals a game for the Cardinals, who finished the season with a 30–10 record. <ref>{{cite web|author=Mon, Apr 8 |url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/45951/peyton-siva |title=Peyton Siva Stats, News, Videos, Highlights, Pictures, Bio – Louisville Cardinals – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=1990-10-24 |accessdate=2013-04-09}}</ref>

===Senior year===
[[Image:Russ Smith Peyton Siva championship trophy.jpg|thumb|right|200px|[[Russ Smith (basketball)|Russ Smith]] (left) and Siva (right) with the [[2013 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]] trophy.]]
Before the start of the [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13 basketball season]] the [[2012–13 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team]] was picked to finish 1st in the [[2012–13 Big East Conference men's basketball season|Big East Conference]] in polls done by Big East writers <ref>{{cite web|author=Central New York |url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2012/10/louisville_tops_big_east_write.html |title=Louisville tops Big East writers' poll; Cardinals dominate all-league teams |publisher=syracuse.com |date= |accessdate=2013-04-09}}</ref> and coaches. <ref>{{cite web|last=Smith |first=Jared |url=http://newyork.sbnation.com/2012/10/17/3517762/big-east-basketball-media-day-2012-coaches-poll-all-big-east-preseason |title=Big East basketball media day: Coaches' poll, All-Big East preseason teams and news – SB Nation New York |publisher=Newyork.sbnation.com |date=2012-10-17 |accessdate=2013-04-09}}</ref> Siva was selected as the Big East Preseason Player of the Year and to the Big East Preseason first team by both the writers and coaches also. U of L finished the regular season with a 26–5 record and 14–4 in the Big East to tie for a share of the Big East regular season championship with [[2012–13 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|Georgetown]] and [[2012–13 Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Marquette]], who also finished with a 14–4 conference record. <ref>{{cite web|last=Ennis |first=Mark |url=http://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2013/3/12/4091940/2013-big-east-tournament-preview-louisville-georgetown-syracuse-otto-porter |title=2013 Big East Tournament preview: Louisville and Georgetown favorites in league's swan song |publisher=SBNation.com |date=2013-03-12 |accessdate=2013-04-09}}</ref>  Siva led Louisville to the [[2013 Big East Men's Basketball Tournament|2013 Big East Tournament]] championship and was named the tournament's most outstanding player for the second consecutive year. Siva became the second player ever to win this award multiple times; [[Patrick Ewing]] accomplished the same feat in 1984 and 1985<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2013/03/louisvilles_peyton_siva_joins.html|title=Louisville's Peyton Siva joins Georgetown's Patrick Ewing as the only two-time winners of the Big East Most Outstanding Player award|publisher=Syracuse Post-Standard}}</ref> Siva had a Big East tournament and school record for steals in a Big East tournament game with seven vs [[2012–13 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|Notre Dame]] in the semi-finals, it tied [[Terrence Williams]] (also from Seattle, WA) the only other Louisville player and 10 others. <ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gocards.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/031613aaf.html |title=Louisville-Notre Dame Postgame Notes – Louisville Cardinals Official Athletic Site |publisher=Gocards.com |date= |accessdate=2013-04-09}}</ref> The seven steals made him Louisville's all-time career leader with 236 steals, at that time, he passed [[Darrell Griffith]]’s record of 230 he had from 1976–80. <ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=330740097 |title=Notre Dame Fighting Irish vs. Louisville Cardinals – Recap – March 15, 2013 – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=2013-03-15 |accessdate=2013-04-09}}</ref> Louisville, with a 29–5 record, was selected the #1 overall seed for the [[2013 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2013 NCAA Tournament]]. <ref>{{cite overall seed – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=2013-03-26 |accessdate=2013-04-09}}</ref> Siva was a 2012–13 [[Academic All-America]] selection.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cosida.com/news.aspx?id=3973|title=Delaware's Elena Delle Donne, Ohio State's Aaron Craft top Capital One Academic All-America® Division I Basketball ==Personal life==
Siva is a devout Christian and is involved with Louisville's Fellowship of Christian Athletes. After Siva successfully talked his father out of suicide, the two have become close, according to the younger Siva. His father gave up other drugs shortly after the suicide attempt; while he has continued to struggle with alcohol, family members say his condition has steadily improved.<ref name=Saslow/> Every year during his son's career at Louisville, his father came to Louisville to spend the season with his son, and was a fixture at Cardinals home games.<ref name=Saslow/> His siblings have also abandoned their previous criminal activity, and his mother, who had worked three jobs while he was growing up, is now a drug counselor.<ref name=Saslow/> Peyton is now one of the top searched college basketball players this season.<ref>{{cite web|author=Lisa Olson |url=http://aol.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2012-03-14/ncaa-tournament-2012-louisville-guard-peyton-sivas-most-important-drive-came-off |title=Louisville guard Peyton Siva Jr.'s most important drive came off the court – NCAA Basketball – Sporting News |publisher=Aol.sportingnews.com |date=2012-03-14 |accessdate=2013-04-09}}</ref>
